+def _assert_scorer(case, logits, counts, lens, *, top_k=TOP_K, scale=None, table=None):
+    """The scorer's contract on one case: counts = the oracle's visible count per row, block_lens = min(top_k, counts), every visible
+    column within the fp32 budget of the fp64 reference, every other column still the sentinel."""
+    scale = D**-0.5 if scale is None else scale
+    n_vis = case.n_vis()
+    _, want_counts = full_block_ids(case.positions(), case.n_blocks_max, BS)  # the oracle's count rule at the capacity: min(capacity, floor((p + 1) / 4))
+    assert torch.equal(counts, want_counts.view(-1).to(torch.int32)), "counts differ from the oracle's count rule"
+    assert torch.equal(counts, n_vis.view(-1).to(torch.int32))
+    if lens is not None:
+        assert torch.equal(lens, torch.minimum(counts, torch.full_like(counts, top_k))), "block_lens differs from min(top_k, counts)"
+    ref = case.reference(scale, table)
+    for b in range(case.batch):
+        for s in range(case.s_q):
+            n = int(n_vis[b, s])
+            row = logits[b * case.s_q + s]
+            if n:
+                torch.testing.assert_close(
+                    row[:n].double(), ref[b, s, :n], atol=LOGIT_ATOL, rtol=LOGIT_RTOL, msg=f"sequence {b} row {s}: logits off the fp64 reference"
+                )
+            assert bool((row[n:] == SENTINEL).all()), f"sequence {b} row {s}: a column at or past the visible count {n} was written"
+
+
+def _assert_rows(block_ids, scores, block_lens, ref, top_k, tie_tol=TIE_TOL):
+    """Per row of ``ref [rows, n_blocks_max]`` (the dense decode selector's oracle): the valid count equals ``block_lens`` =
+    ``min(top_k, visible)``, ids are unique local ids below the visible count, the scores are the reference scores of the selected
+    ids (fp32 of an fp64 value), and the SET equals torch.topk's up to flips within ``tie_tol`` of the k-th reference score."""
+    rows, n_blocks_max = ref.shape
+    assert block_ids.shape == scores.shape == (rows, top_k)
+    assert block_ids.dtype == torch.int32 and scores.dtype == torch.float32 and block_lens.dtype == torch.int32
+    valid = block_ids >= 0
+    visible = torch.isfinite(ref).sum(dim=-1)
+    assert torch.equal(valid.sum(dim=-1).to(torch.int32), block_lens), "the valid prefix differs from block_lens"
+    assert torch.equal(block_lens.long(), visible.clamp(max=top_k)), "block_lens differs from min(top_k, visible)"
+    prefix = torch.arange(top_k, device=ref.device)[None, :] < block_lens[:, None].long()
+    assert torch.equal(valid, prefix), "the valid ids are not a prefix followed by -1"
+    assert bool(((block_ids < visible[:, None]) | ~valid).all()), "an id at or past the row's visible count"
+    assert bool(torch.isneginf(scores[~valid]).all())
+    row_idx = torch.arange(rows, device=ref.device).unsqueeze(1).expand_as(block_ids)
+    gathered = ref[row_idx[valid], block_ids[valid].long()]
+    torch.testing.assert_close(scores[valid].double(), gathered, atol=tie_tol, rtol=tie_tol)
+    in_actual = torch.zeros_like(ref, dtype=torch.bool)
+    in_actual[row_idx[valid], block_ids[valid].long()] = True
+    assert torch.equal(in_actual.sum(dim=-1), valid.sum(dim=-1)), "a row lists a block twice"
+    k_eff = min(top_k, n_blocks_max)
+    ref_topk = torch.topk(ref, k_eff, dim=-1)
+    exp_valid = torch.isfinite(ref_topk.values)
+    in_expected = torch.zeros_like(in_actual)
+    rows_k = torch.arange(rows, device=ref.device).unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, k_eff)
+    in_expected[rows_k[exp_valid], ref_topk.indices[exp_valid]] = True
+    kth = torch.where(exp_valid, ref_topk.values, torch.full_like(ref_topk.values, float("inf"))).min(dim=-1).values
+    differs = in_actual ^ in_expected
+    if bool(differs.any()):
+        gap = (ref - kth.unsqueeze(1)).abs()[differs]
+        assert bool((gap <= tie_tol).all()), f"{int(differs.sum())} ids differ from torch.topk beyond a tie (max gap {float(gap.max()):.3e})"
+
+
+def _assert_canonical(block_ids, block_lens):
+    """The selected ids come back in ASCENDING order (the deterministic radix kernel's canonical order), the padding last."""
+    for r in range(block_ids.shape[0]):
+        n = int(block_lens[r])
+        ids = block_ids[r, :n]
+        assert bool((ids[1:] > ids[:-1]).all()), f"row {r}: the selected ids are not strictly ascending"
+        assert bool((block_ids[r, n:] == -1).all()), f"row {r}: a non -1 entry past block_lens"
+
+
+def _step_kv_lens(n_blocks_max, rows, batch=4):
+    """Step-0 positions covering every residue modulo the block size, the last sequence seeing every block of the cache."""
+    base = BS * n_blocks_max - rows - 3
+    return [max(0, base + r) + rows for r in range(batch)]

+        assert bool((row[40:48] == 0.0).all()), "a dead page under visible blocks did not read as zero keys"
+        keep = torch.ones(n_blocks_max, dtype=torch.bool, device=_DEV)
+        keep[40:48] = False
+        assert torch.equal(_bits(row[keep]), _bits(logits[4 * rows + s][keep])), "a dead page changed another column"
+    assert torch.equal(counts, counts_c) and torch.equal(lens, lens_c)
+
+
+@needs_scorer
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "h_i,s_q,n_blocks_max,page_size", [(1, 20, 72, 16), (2, 3, 72, 32), (3, 2, 136, 16), (8, 2, 72, 16), (16, 3, 72, 64), (17, 2, 136, 16), (4, 5, 136, 8)]
+)
+def test_scorer_row_map_branches_match_the_fp64_reference(h_i, s_q, n_blocks_max, page_size):
+    """Every branch of the row map against the same fp64 reference: ``P' = 1`` (two queries per lane, no sum), the pair-only sum
+    (``H_i`` 2), a padded head count (3 -> 4), two and three shuffle stages (8 / 16 heads), a query spanning two m-tiles (17 heads),
+    several m-tiles of queries (``s_q`` 20 at one head, 5 at four) -- counts, sentinel and a second launch bitwise."""
+    kv = [4 * n_blocks_max + s_q - 1, 4 * 30 + s_q + 2, s_q]
+    case = _Case(3, s_q, n_blocks_max, page_size, kv, seed=100 * h_i + s_q, h=h_i)
+    r = sp.compile_qsa_score_paged(h_i=h_i, s_q=s_q, page_size=page_size)
+    logits, counts, lens = case.run(r)
+    _assert_scorer(case, logits, counts, lens)
+    logits2, counts2, lens2 = case.run(r)
+    assert torch.equal(_bits(logits), _bits(logits2)) and torch.equal(counts, counts2) and torch.equal(lens, lens2)
+
+
+@needs_scorer
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("page_size", [16, 64])
+def test_units_per_warp_is_a_knob(page_size):
+    """32 / 64 / 128 / 256 compressed rows per warp: the same MMA chain per key whichever warp owns it, so the logits are BITWISE across
+    the knob (the capacity is not a multiple of 1024: every value walks a ragged last chunk)."""
+    case = _Case(3, 2, 1032, page_size, [4 * 1032 - 1, 4 * 700 + 2, 4 * 3 + 3], seed=6)
+    outs = []
+    for units in fd.UNITS_PER_WARP_CHOICES:
+        r = sp.compile_qsa_score_paged(h_i=H, s_q=2, page_size=page_size, units_per_warp=units)
+        outs.append(case.run(r))
+    _assert_scorer(case, *outs[0])
+    for logits, counts, lens in outs[1:]:
+        assert torch.equal(_bits(outs[0][0]), _bits(logits)) and torch.equal(outs[0][1], counts) and torch.equal(outs[0][2], lens)
+
+
+@needs_scorer
+def test_ring_depth_is_a_knob():
+    """2 / 4 / 8 n-tiles of keys in flight per warp: the same copies and the same MMA chain per key, so the logits are BITWISE
+    across the knob; the recipe records the depth and the compile key keeps the default's identity."""
+    case = _Case(2, 3, 1032, 16, [4 * 1032 - 1, 4 * 300 + 2], seed=21)
+    outs = []
+    for depth in fd.RING_DEPTH_CHOICES:
+        r = sp.compile_qsa_score_paged(h_i=H, s_q=3, page_size=16, units_per_warp=2, ring_depth=depth)
+        assert r.ring_depth == depth
+        outs.append(case.run(r))
+    _assert_scorer(case, *outs[0])
+    for logits, counts, lens in outs[1:]:
+        assert torch.equal(_bits(outs[0][0]), _bits(logits)) and torch.equal(outs[0][1], counts) and torch.equal(outs[0][2], lens)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="ring_depth must be one of"):
+        sp.compile_qsa_score_paged(h_i=H, s_q=3, page_size=16, units_per_warp=2, ring_depth=5)
+

+@needs_scorer
+def test_block_lens_output_is_optional_and_the_artifact_pins_its_presence():
+    case = _Case(2, 2, 64, 32, [4 * 64 - 1, 4 * 10], seed=8)
+    with_lens = sp.compile_qsa_score_paged(h_i=H, s_q=2, page_size=32, has_block_lens=True)
+    without = sp.compile_qsa_score_paged(h_i=H, s_q=2, page_size=32, has_block_lens=False)
+    logits_a, counts_a, lens_a = case.run(with_lens)
+    logits_b, counts_b, lens_b = case.run(without, with_lens=False)
+    assert lens_b is None and torch.equal(_bits(logits_a), _bits(logits_b)) and torch.equal(counts_a, counts_b)
+    _assert_scorer(case, logits_a, counts_a, lens_a)
+    logits, counts, lens = case.outputs()
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="compiled without block_lens"):
+        sp.run_qsa_score_paged(without, case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, logits, counts, lens, top_k=TOP_K, scale=D**-0.5, stream=_stream())
+

+@needs_scorer
+@needs_pdl
+def test_use_pdl_arm_is_bitwise_the_plain_launch():
+    """The programmatic-dependent-launch pair (the wait ahead of every global read, the release after the staging) changes the
+    schedule only: logits, counts and block_lens bitwise the plain launch."""
+    case = _Case(3, 4, 2048, 16, [4 * 2048, 4 * 600 + 1, 0], seed=9)
+    plain = sp.compile_qsa_score_paged(h_i=H, s_q=4, page_size=16, use_pdl=False)
+    pdl = sp.compile_qsa_score_paged(h_i=H, s_q=4, page_size=16, use_pdl=True)
+    assert pdl.use_pdl and not plain.use_pdl
+    a = case.run(plain)
+    b = case.run(pdl)
+    _assert_scorer(case, *a)

+
+@needs_scorer
+def test_scale_scales_the_logits_and_a_strided_query_slab_reads_in_place():
+    """``scale`` multiplies every logit (the ordering is scale-free); a column slice of a wider bf16 slab (the band's layout) is
+    read in place -- bitwise the compact copy."""
+    case = _Case(2, 2, 64, 16, [4 * 64 - 1, 4 * 10 + 2], seed=10)
+    r = sp.compile_qsa_score_paged(h_i=H, s_q=2, page_size=16)
+    one = case.run(r, scale=1.0)
+    half = case.run(r, scale=0.5)
+    _assert_scorer(case, *one, scale=1.0)
+    _assert_scorer(case, *half, scale=0.5)
+    slab = torch.zeros(case.qi.shape[0], 640, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=_DEV)
+    slab[:, 64 : 64 + H * D] = case.qi.view(case.qi.shape[0], H * D)
+    strided = slab[:, 64 : 64 + H * D].view(case.qi.shape[0], H, D)
+    assert strided.data_ptr() == slab.data_ptr() + 128 and strided.stride(0) == 640
+    logits, counts, lens = case.outputs()
+    sp.run_qsa_score_paged(r, strided, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, logits, counts, lens, top_k=TOP_K, scale=1.0, stream=_stream())
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(_bits(logits), _bits(one[0])) and torch.equal(counts, one[1])
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- the selector (cc 9.0+)
+
+
+@needs_selector
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("page_size", [16, 32, 64])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", [1, 2, 3, 4])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("n_blocks_max", [8, 520, 4096, 8192, 32768])
+def test_paged_selection_matches_the_fp64_topk_set_up_to_ties(n_blocks_max, rows, page_size):
+    """The standalone selector: every row's SET equals torch.topk of the fp64 reference up to ties, the ids ascending with -1 past
+    block_lens = min(top_k, counts), the counts the oracle's count rule, the scores the reference scores of the selected ids; the
+    identity region (fewer than top_k visible blocks) selects every visible block; two calls BITWISE."""
+    case = _Case(4, rows, n_blocks_max, page_size, _step_kv_lens(n_blocks_max, rows), seed=n_blocks_max + 11 * rows + page_size)
+    # the capacity is passed where the table's reach (whole pages) exceeds it (8 blocks on a 16-row page); where it equals, the default is exercised
+    cap = dict(n_blocks_max=n_blocks_max) if case.max_pages * case.rpp != n_blocks_max else {}
+    out = fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, seq_q=rows, **cap)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    t = 4 * rows
+    assert out["block_ids"].shape == (t, TOP_K) and out["scores"].shape == (t, TOP_K) and out["logits"].shape == (t, n_blocks_max)
+    assert out["counts"].shape == (t,) and out["block_lens"].shape == (t,)
+    _, want_counts = full_block_ids(case.positions(), n_blocks_max, BS)
+    assert torch.equal(out["counts"], want_counts.view(-1).to(torch.int32))
+    ref = case.reference(D**-0.5).view(t, n_blocks_max)
+    _assert_rows(out["block_ids"], out["scores"], out["block_lens"], ref, TOP_K)
+    _assert_canonical(out["block_ids"], out["block_lens"])
+    if n_blocks_max <= TOP_K:
+        want_ids, want_lens = full_block_ids(case.positions(), TOP_K, BS)
+        assert torch.equal(out["block_ids"], want_ids.view(t, TOP_K).to(torch.int32)) and torch.equal(out["block_lens"], want_lens.view(-1).to(torch.int32))
+    again = fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, seq_q=rows, **cap)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    for key in ("block_ids", "counts", "block_lens"):
+        assert torch.equal(out[key], again[key]), f"two calls differ in {key}"
+    assert torch.equal(_bits(out["scores"]), _bits(again["scores"]))
+    live = torch.arange(n_blocks_max, device=_DEV)[None, :] < out["counts"][:, None]
+    assert torch.equal(_bits(out["logits"][live]), _bits(again["logits"][live]))
+
+
+@needs_selector
+def test_selector_preallocated_outputs_are_written_in_place_and_match():
+    case = _Case(3, 2, 1024, 32, [4 * 1024 - 1, 4 * 300 + 2, 0], seed=12)
+    t = 6
+    logits = torch.full((t, 1024), SENTINEL, dtype=torch.float32, device=_DEV)
+    counts = torch.full((t,), -7, dtype=torch.int32, device=_DEV)
+    lens = torch.full((t,), -7, dtype=torch.int32, device=_DEV)
+    out = fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, seq_q=2, logits_out=logits, counts_out=counts, block_lens_out=lens)
+    base = fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, seq_q=2)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert out["logits"].data_ptr() == logits.data_ptr() and out["counts"].data_ptr() == counts.data_ptr() and out["block_lens"].data_ptr() == lens.data_ptr()
+    _assert_scorer(case, logits, counts, lens)
+    assert torch.equal(out["block_ids"], base["block_ids"]) and torch.equal(_bits(out["scores"]), _bits(base["scores"]))
+    assert counts[4:].tolist() == [0, 0] and bool((out["block_ids"][4:] == -1).all()) and bool(torch.isneginf(out["scores"][4:]).all())
+
+
+@needs_selector
+def test_selector_knobs_are_the_same_function():
+    """``units_per_warp`` and ``use_pdl`` (cc 9.0+) are performance knobs of the selector: block_ids and scores bitwise."""
+    case = _Case(2, 3, 4096, 16, [4 * 4096 - 2, 4 * 1000 + 1], seed=13)
+    base = fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, seq_q=3)
+    for kw in (dict(units_per_warp=1), dict(units_per_warp=4), dict(use_pdl=True)):
+        other = fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, seq_q=3, **kw)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.equal(base["block_ids"], other["block_ids"]) and torch.equal(_bits(base["scores"]), _bits(other["scores"])), kw
+
+
+@needs_selector
+def test_selector_on_a_side_stream_with_the_ambient_stream_parked_matches_the_synchronised_control():
+    """The delayed-producer pin with the REAL kernels (Rule 5): a synchronised control on torch's default stream first (it compiles both
+    kernels, so the parked window below holds launches only); then the default (ambient) stream is parked by a long spin and the SAME
+    selection is issued on a side stream, passed as a ``torch.cuda.Stream``; the side stream ALONE is synchronised and the outputs are
+    compared ON the side stream while the ambient stream is still parked -- anything the call had wrongly enqueued on the ambient
+    stream (an allocation's fill, the top-k, a copy) would not have run yet, and the comparison would see it.  block_ids, scores,
+    counts, block_lens and the live logits bitwise the control; the premise -- the ambient stream busy at the issue and at the
+    comparison -- is asserted."""
+    if not hasattr(torch.cuda, "_sleep"):
+        pytest.skip("torch.cuda._sleep is the park; the matmul fallback is too short")
+    from gated_block_stream_probe import park_the_default_stream
+
+    case = _Case(3, 2, 4096, 16, [4 * 4096 - 2, 4 * 1000 + 1, 4 * 20 + 2], seed=16)
+    ambient, side = torch.cuda.default_stream(), torch.cuda.Stream()
+    assert torch.cuda.current_stream() == ambient and side != ambient
+    control = fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, seq_q=2)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    ref = case.reference(D**-0.5).view(6, 4096)
+    _assert_rows(control["block_ids"], control["scores"], control["block_lens"], ref, TOP_K)
+    park_the_default_stream(3.0)  # the AMBIENT stream is busy from here, through the call and past the comparison
+    out = fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, seq_q=2, stream=side)
+    parked_at_issue = not ambient.query()
+    side.synchronize()  # the LAUNCH stream only
+    with torch.cuda.stream(side):
+        same = {key: torch.equal(out[key], control[key]) for key in ("block_ids", "counts", "block_lens")}
+        same["scores"] = torch.equal(_bits(out["scores"]), _bits(control["scores"]))
+        live = torch.arange(4096, device=_DEV)[None, :] < control["counts"][:, None]
+        same["logits"] = torch.equal(_bits(out["logits"][live]), _bits(control["logits"][live]))
+    parked_at_compare = not ambient.query()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    print(f"premise: parked_at_issue={parked_at_issue} parked_at_compare={parked_at_compare}; same={same}")
+    assert parked_at_issue and parked_at_compare, "the premise: the ambient stream must still be busy at the issue and at the comparison"
+    assert all(same.values()), f"the selection on the side stream differs from the synchronised control: {same}"
+
+
+@needs_selector
+def test_paged_entry_agrees_with_the_dense_selector_when_that_module_is_present():
+    """The dense-cache decode selector (``cudnn.gated_attention_block.qsa_select``) is a sibling change: probed BY NAME -- skipped by
+    name where the tree lacks it, imported unguarded where it is present -- then both selectors over the same keys (the dense form
+    through the gathered cache) select the same SET per row up to ties at the k-th boundary."""
+    if importlib.util.find_spec("cudnn.gated_attention_block.qsa_select") is None:
+        pytest.skip("the dense decode selector module cudnn.gated_attention_block.qsa_select is absent from this tree (a sibling change)")
+    dense_mod = importlib.import_module("cudnn.gated_attention_block.qsa_select")
+    rows, n_blocks_max = 4, 2048
+    case = _Case(3, rows, n_blocks_max, 16, [4 * 1500 + 1 + rows, 4 * 2000 + 3 + rows, 4 * 300 + rows], seed=14)
+    paged = fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, seq_q=rows)
+    try:
+        dense = dense_mod.qsa_select_decode(case.qi.view(3, rows, H, D), case.dense().contiguous(), case.kv_lens, list_per_sequence=False)
+    except NotImplementedError as error:
+        pytest.skip(f"the dense selector declines on this device: {error}")
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    ref = case.reference(D**-0.5).view(-1, n_blocks_max)
+    dense_ids = dense["block_ids"].view(-1, TOP_K)

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""``qsa_score_paged`` -- the decode indexer's scorer over the PAGED compressed-key cache; its standalone selector is the host entry
+``gated_attention_block/qsa_select_paged.py``.
+
+A decode step of a block-sparse (``QsaSpec``) layer scores each of its ``S_q`` query rows per sequence against the compressed
+keys of the complete 4-token blocks the row can see, and the top-k of those scores is the row's block list.  The serving
+stacks keep the compressed keys PAGED on the main block table (one compressed row per 4 tokens, ``page_size / 4`` rows per
+page), so this kernel reads them there -- once, in page order, never through a dense per-sequence copy::
+
+    pos_t   = kv_lens[b] - S_q + s                       (row s of sequence b; t = b * S_q + s)
+    n_vis_t = clamp(floor((pos_t + 1) / 4), 0, n_blocks_max)
+    logits[t, j] = scale * sum_h relu(qi[t, h] . kbar[b, j])        for j < n_vis_t, kbar[b, j] = cache[table[b, j // R], j % R]
+    counts[t]     = n_vis_t                                          (R = page_size / 4 compressed rows per page)
+    block_lens[t] = min(top_k, n_vis_t)                              (optional output)
+
+The ``logits [T, n_blocks_max]`` fp32 + ``counts [T]`` int32 pair is the input contract of the decode top-k that follows
+(the radix kernel today, a FROST top-k later): the top-k reads row ``t``'s columns ``[0, counts[t])`` -- nothing else of the
+row is written here -- and pads its output with ``-1`` past ``min(top_k, counts[t])``.  The host entry
+``qsa_select_paged.qsa_select_decode_paged`` (a DSL-free module, so its import path resolves on every installed DSL) pairs the
+scorer with the deterministic radix top-k (the smaller block id wins a tie at the cutoff, the selected ids come back in ASCENDING
+order, so two calls are bitwise) and no torch prologue: the positions and the counts are derived on device by this kernel.
+
+**The form: a warp-level MMA over the (s, h) columns, the keys streamed by ``cp.async``.**  A decode step has 1-4 query rows per
+sequence, 4 indexer heads each: the ``S_q x H_i`` (s, h) rows pad to the M = 16 of one ``mma.sync.m16n8k16`` (bf16 in, fp32
+accumulate), so one MMA per 8 keys per 16 of the 128 D scores EVERY column at once -- the work is flat in ``S_q`` and the compute
+term is negligible against the bytes (131 k MAC per 16 KB of keys).  The padded query tile is staged ONCE per CTA in shared memory
+(``cp.async``, every thread a 16-B granule, zero-fill for the padding rows) behind the kernel's one CTA barrier and read into A
+fragments; the keys stream through a per-warp ring of ``cp.async`` groups -- page part by page part, whole 128-B lines per
+request, an L2 evict-first policy (the keys pass through L2 once; the logits' write-combining lines and the table stay), a
+zero-filled copy for a dead page -- into B fragments read with ``ld.shared.v4``; relu, the head sum and the scale run on the fp32
+accumulator fragment.  No TMA, no TMEM, no cluster: the first key byte is requested ONE memory round trip after the launch
+(``kv_lens``, the table words and the query tile are all in flight together), nothing holds a register while it waits, and the
+kernel's roofline term is the HBM bytes of the compressed rows it streams (plus the fp32 logits it writes).
+
+Work decomposition (every constant below is a module constant or a compile key; nothing is inferred at launch):
+
+* grid ``(ceil(n_blocks_max / blocks_per_cta), B)``, CTA = 4 warps = 128 threads; a warp owns ``keys_per_warp = 32 x
+  units_per_warp`` consecutive compressed rows (``units_per_warp`` in {1, 2, 4, 8} is a performance knob: the same function;
+  ``blocks_per_cta`` = 128 / 256 / 512 / 1024; the default 1 = the best point of every measured cell), streamed as n-tiles of 8
+  keys, ``ring_depth`` (2 / 4 / 8, default 4: a performance knob) n-tiles in flight;
+* **the K permutation** shared by A and B (so the product is unchanged): lane ``(g = lane / 4, q = lane % 4)`` reads the 16-byte
+  granules ``c = q + 4 j`` (``j = 0..3``) of its row, and k-step ``kappa = 2 j + r`` takes granule ``q + 4 j``'s words ``2 r`` (logical k
+  ``2q, 2q + 1``) and ``2 r + 1`` (logical k ``2q + 8, 2q + 9``): a bijection ``(kappa, k) <-> D``, so the fragment registers ARE the
+  granules' words (no shuffle, no ``ldmatrix``).  A per m-tile: ``reg0 / reg1`` = rows ``g`` / ``g + 8`` at word ``2 r``, ``reg2 /
+  reg3`` the same rows at word ``2 r + 1``; B per n-tile: key ``n = g``'s words ``2 r`` / ``2 r + 1``; C: lane ``(g, q)`` holds rows
+  ``g`` / ``g + 8`` for keys ``2q, 2q + 1``;
+* **the row map** (``qsa_select_paged.query_row_map``): a query's heads pad to ``P = next_pow2(H_i)`` rows; ``P' = min(P, 16)``
+  of them share a 16-row m-tile with ``QPT = 16 / P'`` queries, a query wider than a tile spans ``TPQ = P / 16`` tiles
+  (``m_tiles = ceil(S_q x P / 16) <= 4``, the ``MAX_QUERY_ROWS`` envelope); with ``P' >= 2`` the two rows a lane holds are heads
+  ``2 gi`` / ``2 gi + 1`` of ONE query (``gi = g % G``, ``G = P' / 2``) and the remaining heads sit in the ``G`` consecutive ``g``
+  values = lanes ``xor 4, 8, 16``: the head sum is one in-thread add plus ``log2(G)`` butterfly shuffles (H_i 4: ONE), plus the
+  in-thread sums over a query's tiles at ``P > 16``; with ``P' = 1`` the two rows are two queries and nothing is summed; a padding
+  row (``h >= H_i`` inside the power of two, ``s >= S_q``) is a ZERO row of the staged tile (its copy is zero-filled);
+* the prologue, every thread: ``kv_lens[b]``; the table words of the first ``2 x ring_depth`` n-tiles (per lane the word of ITS key,
+  ``table[b, min(k, n_blocks_max - 1) / R]``: 1-4 distinct words per instruction, one sector); the query tile's copies (2 per m-tile,
+  one ``cp.async`` group); then -- live warps only (``k_warp0 < n_vis_max``, warp-uniform) -- the first ``ring_depth`` n-tiles of
+  keys (one group each); ``cp.async.wait_group`` for the query tile's group; the CTA barrier; the A fragments (8 ``ld.shared.v4``
+  per m-tile per lane);
+* the mainloop, live warps, in batches of ``mma_batch`` n-tiles (4 at ``units_per_warp`` 1, 2 above: the HMMA chains of a batch
+  interleave) -- per n-tile: the table word of n-tile ``i + 2 x ring_depth``; ``cp.async.wait_group`` for group ``i``; ``bar.warp.sync``

+    kc = k if k < n_blocks_max else n_blocks_max - cutlass.Int32(1)
+    pg = kc >> cutlass.Int32(rows_per_page.bit_length() - 1)
+    return ld_global(tb_row + pg.to(cutlass.Int64) * cutlass.Int64(4), cutlass.Int32)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _mul_wide_s32(a: cutlass.Int32, b: cutlass.Int32) -> cutlass.Int64:
+    """``mul.wide.s32``: one IMAD.WIDE for a 32 x 32 -> 64-bit product (a page index x a page stride in bytes)."""
+    return inline_ptx("mul.wide.s32 $0, $1, $2;", write_only_types=[cutlass.Int64], read_only_args=[a, b])
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _copy_ntile(
+    dst_lane: cutlass.Int64,
+    src_lane_off: cutlass.Int32,
+    kb_base: cutlass.Int64,
+    kb_page_bytes: cutlass.Int32,
+    word: cutlass.Int32,
+    num_pages: cutlass.Int32,
+    k_tile0: cutlass.Int32,
+    policy: cutlass.Int64,
+    rows_per_page: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+):
+    """The n-tile's 8 compressed rows into one ring slot, PAGE PART by page part (``min(R, 8)`` rows of one page): per part ONE
+    shuffle (the part's table word from the lane that read it -- a constant source lane), one validity check, one ``mul.wide``
+    page address; then ``rows / 2`` ``cp.async.cg`` of 16 B per lane at immediate offsets -- instruction ``e`` copies rows ``2 e``
+    (lanes 0-15) and ``2 e + 1`` (lanes 16-31), each row's two 128-B halves by eight consecutive lanes (whole lines per request).
+    A part on a ``-1`` / out-of-range page is ZERO-FILLED (``src-size 0``: nothing of the cache is read; the address is page 0, a
+    real row, either way).  A row at or past the visible count or the capacity reads a real row (its table word was clamped to
+    the capacity) and is never stored: its products stay in its own accumulator column."""
+    rows_pp = min(rows_per_page, KEYS_PER_NTILE)
+    zero_i = cutlass.Int32(0)
+    for part in cutlass.range_constexpr(KEYS_PER_NTILE // rows_pp):
+        w = cute.arch.shuffle_sync(word, 4 * part * rows_pp)  # the word of the part's first row sits in lanes 4 r .. 4 r + 3
+        ok = (w >= zero_i) & (w < num_pages)
+        page_c = w if ok else zero_i
+        size = cutlass.Int32(_CHUNK_BYTES) if ok else zero_i
+        row_off = ((k_tile0 + cutlass.Int32(part * rows_pp)) & cutlass.Int32(rows_per_page - 1)) * cutlass.Int32(
+            _ROW_BYTES
+        )  # the part's first row inside its page
+        src = kb_base + _mul_wide_s32(page_c, kb_page_bytes) + (row_off + src_lane_off).to(cutlass.Int64)
+        dst = dst_lane + cutlass.Int64(part * rows_pp * _ROW_BYTES)
+        for e in cutlass.range_constexpr(rows_pp // 2):
+            # every cp.async gets its OWN address registers (an opaque offset, never base + immediate): four back-to-back LDGSTS on one
+            # base register serialised on the register scoreboard under HBM latency (2x at B 32 x 128K, measured 2026-10-21)
+            off_e = opaque_i32(cutlass.Int32(e * 2 * _ROW_BYTES)).to(cutlass.Int64)
+            inline_ptx(
+                "cp.async.cg.shared.global.L2::cache_hint [$0], [$1], 16, $2, $3;", write_only_types=[], read_only_args=[dst + off_e, src + off_e, size, policy]
+            )
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _read_key_frags(sK, slot_elems: cutlass.Int32, g: cutlass.Int32, qd: cutlass.Int32):
+    """Lane ``(g, q)``'s B fragments of the n-tile in the ring slot: row ``g``'s granules ``q + 4 j`` (one ``ld.shared.v4`` each,
+    at the swizzled granule ``c ^ (4 x (g & 1))``) -- the 16 words the 8 k-steps consume."""
+    swz = (g & cutlass.Int32(1)) * cutlass.Int32(4)
+    row = slot_elems + g * cutlass.Int32(_ROW_BYTES // 4)
+    out = []
+    for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(CHUNKS_PER_LANE):
+        c_swz = (qd + cutlass.Int32(4 * j)) ^ swz
+        v = sK.load(row + c_swz * cutlass.Int32(_WORDS_PER_CHUNK), vector_size=4, alignment=16).to_elements()
+        for x in cutlass.range_constexpr(_WORDS_PER_CHUNK):
+            out.append(v[x])
+    return out[0], out[1], out[2], out[3], out[4], out[5], out[6], out[7], out[8], out[9], out[10], out[11], out[12], out[13], out[14], out[15]
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _copy_query_tile(
+    sA_tile: cutlass.Int64,
+    q_base: cutlass.Int64,
+    q_s0: cutlass.Int64,
+    q_s1: cutlass.Int64,
+    t0: cutlass.Int32,
+    tidx: cutlass.Int32,
+    t: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    s_q: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    h_i: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+):
+    """m-tile ``t`` of the padded (s, h) query tile into the CTA's SMEM staging: 16 rows x 256 B by the 128 threads in two
+    ``cp.async.cg`` instructions (thread ``tidx`` copies granule ``tidx % 16`` of rows ``tidx / 16`` and ``8 + tidx / 16``: sixteen
+    consecutive lanes per row, whole lines); a padding row (``h >= H_i`` inside the power of two, ``s >= S_q``) is ZERO-FILLED
+    (``src-size 0``; its address is a real row).  The destination granule is ``c ^ (4 x (row & 1))``, the fragment reads' swizzle."""
+    rm = query_row_map(s_q, h_i)
+    zero_i = cutlass.Int32(0)
+    s_q_i = cutlass.Int32(s_q)
+    h_i_i = cutlass.Int32(h_i)
+    c = tidx & cutlass.Int32(15)
+    g = tidx >> cutlass.Int32(4)  # the row within the half: 0..7
+    for half in cutlass.range_constexpr(2):
+        if cutlass.const_expr(rm.tile_rows == 1):
+            s_row = cutlass.Int32(t * rm.queries_per_tile + 8 * half) + g
+            h_row = zero_i
+        else:
+            s_row = cutlass.Int32((t // rm.tiles_per_query) * rm.queries_per_tile) + (g >> cutlass.Int32(rm.stages))
+            h_row = cutlass.Int32(16 * (t % rm.tiles_per_query) + half) + (g & cutlass.Int32(rm.group - 1)) * cutlass.Int32(2)
+        valid = (s_row < s_q_i) & (h_row < h_i_i)
+        s_c = s_row if s_row < s_q_i else s_q_i - cutlass.Int32(1)
+        h_c = h_row if h_row < h_i_i else h_i_i - cutlass.Int32(1)
+        src = (
+            q_base + ((t0 + s_c).to(cutlass.Int64) * q_s0 + h_c.to(cutlass.Int64) * q_s1) * cutlass.Int64(2) + c.to(cutlass.Int64) * cutlass.Int64(_CHUNK_BYTES)
+        )
+        dst = sA_tile + (
+            cutlass.Int32(half * 8 * _ROW_BYTES)
+            + g * cutlass.Int32(_ROW_BYTES)
+            + (c ^ ((g & cutlass.Int32(1)) * cutlass.Int32(4))) * cutlass.Int32(_CHUNK_BYTES)
+        ).to(cutlass.Int64)
+        size = cutlass.Int32(_CHUNK_BYTES) if valid else zero_i
+        inline_ptx("cp.async.cg.shared.global [$0], [$1], 16, $2;", write_only_types=[], read_only_args=[dst, src, size])
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _read_query_frags(sA, tile_elems: cutlass.Int32, g: cutlass.Int32, qd: cutlass.Int32, half: cutlass.Constexpr[int]):
+    """Lane ``(g, q)``'s A fragments of one half (rows ``g`` / ``g + 8``) of an m-tile: granules ``q + 4 j`` of the row (one
+    ``ld.shared.v4`` each at the swizzled granule ``c ^ (4 x (row & 1))``) -- the 16 words the 8 k-steps consume."""
+    row = cutlass.Int32(half * 8) + g
+    swz = (row & cutlass.Int32(1)) * cutlass.Int32(4)
+    base = tile_elems + row * cutlass.Int32(_ROW_BYTES // 4)
+    out = []
+    for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(CHUNKS_PER_LANE):
+        c_swz = (qd + cutlass.Int32(4 * j)) ^ swz
+        v = sA.load(base + c_swz * cutlass.Int32(_WORDS_PER_CHUNK), vector_size=4, alignment=16).to_elements()
+        for x in cutlass.range_constexpr(_WORDS_PER_CHUNK):
+            out.append(v[x])
+    return out[0], out[1], out[2], out[3], out[4], out[5], out[6], out[7], out[8], out[9], out[10], out[11], out[12], out[13], out[14], out[15]
+
+
+@cute.kernel
+def frost_qsa_score_paged(
+    mQ: cute.Tensor,  # [T, H_i, D] bf16; token / head strides symbolic (Int64), D contiguous
+    mKbar: cute.Tensor,  # [num_pages, R, D] bf16; page / row strides symbolic (Int64), D contiguous
+    mTable: cute.Tensor,  # [B, max_pages] int32; row stride symbolic (Int64), unit column stride
+    mKvLens: cute.Tensor,  # [B] int32, contiguous
+    mLogits: cute.Tensor,  # [T, n_blocks_max] fp32; row stride symbolic (Int64), unit column stride
+    mCounts: cute.Tensor,  # [T] int32, contiguous
+    mBlockLens: Optional[cute.Tensor],  # [T] int32, contiguous, or None (folded out)
+    top_k: cutlass.Int32,
+    scale: cutlass.Float32,
+    h_i: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    s_q: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    rows_per_page: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    units_per_warp: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    ring_depth: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    use_pdl: cutlass.Constexpr[bool],
+) -> None:
+    """One CTA = chunk ``blockIdx.x`` of ``blocks_per_cta`` compressed rows of sequence ``blockIdx.y``, four independent warps of
+    ``keys_per_warp`` rows each (module docstring)."""
+    if cutlass.const_expr(use_pdl):
+        wait_on_dependent_grids()
+    rm = query_row_map(s_q, h_i)  # the (s, h) -> MMA-row map (host facts, compile-time)
+    n_tiles = NTILES_PER_UNIT * units_per_warp  # n-tiles of 8 keys per warp
+    depth = ring_depth  # n-tiles of keys in flight (cp.async groups) ahead of the MMAs
+    ring_slots = min(
+        ring_depth + 1, n_tiles
+    )  # + the slot being read (the one warp sync per n-tile orders the WAR on the slot reused next); no spare when no mainloop copy exists
+    # the two SMEM buffers (declared ahead of every branch): each warp's ring of ring_slots n-tiles of 8 compressed rows, and the
+    # CTA's padded (s, h) query tile (16 rows x 256 B per m-tile), both written by cp.async and read as fragments
+    sK = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int32, THREADS // 32 * ring_slots * _SLOT_ELEMS, alignment=128, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem)
+    sA = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int32, rm.m_tiles * _A_TILE_ELEMS, alignment=128, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem)
+    n_groups = rm.m_tiles // rm.tiles_per_query  # query groups per lane at P' >= 2 (one head-sum each)
+    has_lens = cutlass.const_expr(mBlockLens is not None)
+    pair_rows = cutlass.const_expr(rm.tile_rows > 1)  # the lane's two rows are two heads of ONE query (else two queries)

+"""``qsa_score_paged`` -- the decode indexer's scorer over the PAGED compressed-key cache; its standalone selector is the host entry
+``gated_attention_block/qsa_select_paged.py``.

+A decode step of a block-sparse (``QsaSpec``) layer scores each of its ``S_q`` query rows per sequence against the compressed
+keys of the complete 4-token blocks the row can see, and the top-k of those scores is the row's block list.  The serving
+stacks keep the compressed keys PAGED on the main block table (one compressed row per 4 tokens, ``page_size / 4`` rows per
+page), so this kernel reads them there -- once, in page order, never through a dense per-sequence copy::
+
+    pos_t   = kv_lens[b] - S_q + s                       (row s of sequence b; t = b * S_q + s)
+    n_vis_t = clamp(floor((pos_t + 1) / 4), 0, n_blocks_max)
+    logits[t, j] = scale * sum_h relu(qi[t, h] . kbar[b, j])        for j < n_vis_t, kbar[b, j] = cache[table[b, j // R], j % R]
+    counts[t]     = n_vis_t                                          (R = page_size / 4 compressed rows per page)
+    block_lens[t] = min(top_k, n_vis_t)                              (optional output)

+row is written here -- and pads its output with ``-1`` past ``min(top_k, counts[t])``.  The host entry

+``bar.warp.sync``     the warp barrier (``cute.arch.sync_warp``)  all 32 lanes, once per n-tile     32 == the warp       inside the warp-uniform live branch only: after the wait of group ``i``, before the
+                      with memory ordering                                                                              fragment reads of slot ``i`` and the copies into the slot read at step ``i - 1``
+``mma.sync.aligned``  warp-collective                          all 32 lanes, ``8 x m_tiles`` per   32                   inside the live branch only (``k_warp0 < n_vis_max``: both operands warp-uniform)
+                                                              n-tile
+``shfl.sync.bfly``    warp-collective (mask ``0xffffffff``)    all 32 lanes, ``2 x stages`` per     32                   the same branch; the per-lane store predicates come AFTER the shuffles
+                                                              query group per n-tile
+``shfl.sync.idx``     warp-collective (mask ``0xffffffff``)    all 32 lanes, one per page part      32                   the same branch (the copies' table word from a constant source lane)
+====================  ======================================  ==================================  ===================  ===============================================================================
+
+PDL sites (under the ``use_pdl`` compile key, the launch attribute set with it): ``griddepcontrol.wait`` is the kernel's first
+instruction -- ahead of the ``kv_lens`` / table / ``qi`` reads and so of every cache read --, ``griddepcontrol.launch_dependents``
+follows the prologue's copies, BEFORE the counts and the logits are written.  That early trigger puts an obligation on the dependent
+grid: a kernel launched with the programmatic-stream-serialization attribute behind this one may start while this one still runs and
+MUST issue its own ``griddepcontrol.wait`` before it touches anything this kernel reads or writes (``logits``, ``counts``,
+``block_lens``, and the inputs it could overwrite); the wait returns only after this grid has completed and flushed.  The standalone
+selector (``qsa_select_decode_paged``) launches the radix top-k WITHOUT the attribute, so the pair is inert there (the top-k starts
+after the scorer completes, as any stream-ordered launch); it matters in the fused decode chain, whose nodes carry the attribute and
+wait.  Without PDL (``use_pdl=False``, the standalone default) neither instruction is traced and the kernel runs on any CuTe DSL
+device from sm_80 (``mma.sync.m16n8k16``, ``cp.async``).
+
+Degenerate inputs, each with its handling: ``kv_lens[b] == 0`` (a padding sequence) -> every ``pos_t < 0``, ``n_vis = 0``: no
+logits column written, ``counts = block_lens = 0``, no warp of the sequence copies a key (its ``qi`` rows and table words ARE read
+-- valid memory, the round trip that keeps the critical path at two -- and its threads stage the query tile and reach the barrier);
+``kv_lens[b] < S_q`` (a contract violation) -> the rows at a negative position get ``n_vis = 0`` likewise; ``n_vis`` inside a page
+-> the rows past ``n_vis_max`` of a live n-tile read a real row and store nothing (their products stay in their own accumulator
+column); a ``-1`` table entry (or one at or past ``num_pages``) for a VISIBLE block -> the part's copy is zero-filled: logit exactly
+0, still written -- the sparse core's dead-page convention, never an out-of-bounds read; a dead page past ``n_vis_max`` may be
+consulted (its word read, its copy zero-filled or a real page read) and is never stored; fewer than ``top_k`` visible blocks (the
+identity region) -> ``block_lens = n_vis``, the paired top-k lists every visible id ascending then ``-1``; ``n_vis`` past
+``n_blocks_max`` -> clamped to the capacity (the host checks the table's reach ``max_pages x R >= n_blocks_max``; a lane past the
+capacity indexes the table at ``n_blocks_max - 1``).  Refused at the host before any launch: a table narrower than the capacity, a
+page size that is not a power of two (at least 8), ``S_q x next_pow2(H_i)`` past the envelope (``MAX_QUERY_ROWS``), a head dim
+other than 128, a cache whose rows are not contiguous inside a page or whose page stride is 2 GiB or more, misaligned or
+non-unit-stride operands, a mixed dtype pair, and -- by name, a typed ``NotImplementedError`` -- the e4m3 pair (the fp8 indexer
+cache's read arm is a follow-up of this kernel: the bf16 pair is served).
+
+Bytes per launch (the SOL denominator): ``sum_b n_vis_max(b) x 256 B`` of compressed rows read once; ``sum_t n_vis_t x 4 B`` of
+logits written; the query tile per live CTA (``m_tiles x 4 KiB``, L2-resident) and one table word per page --
+``qsa_select_paged.moved_bytes``.
+
+Rule 7: this module imports the DSL at import time like its neighbours, so the documented host entry lives in the DSL-free
+front door ``gated_attention_block/qsa_select_paged.py`` -- ``qsa_select_decode_paged`` gates the DSL floor, the ``sm_107a``
+target on cc 10.7 and the radix top-k's cc 9.0 BEFORE importing this module -- and the kernel's host-side facts (the row map,
+the compile-key validator, the knob defaults, the byte model) are defined there and imported here, never the other way round
+at module scope.  :func:`compile_qsa_score_paged`, the kernel-level entry a caller may reach directly, gates the floor and the
+target again BEFORE any compile, so a too-old DSL reads as a version decline there too; the tests skip below the floor.
+"""
+
+import hashlib
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import NamedTuple, Optional
+
+import cuda.bindings.driver as cuda
+import cutlass
+import cutlass.cute as cute
+import torch
+
+from cudnn.frost.buffers import cutedsl_arch_requirement_error, cutedsl_requirement_error
+from cudnn.frost.compiled_cache import compile_cached, template_key
+from cudnn.frost.device import compute_capability, current_device
+from cudnn.frost.tile_dsl.barrier import launch_dependent_grids, wait_on_dependent_grids
+from cudnn.frost.tile_dsl.mma import mma_m16n8k16_f32
+from cudnn.frost.tile_dsl.pointwise import opaque_f32_zero, opaque_i32
+from cudnn.frost.tile_dsl.tma import ld_global, ld_global_v4, st_global, st_global_v2
+from cutlass.cute.arch.nvvm_wrappers import inline_ptx
+
+# the kernel's host-side facts live in the DSL-free front door (Rule 7: a declaration reads them without importing this module)
+from ..qsa_select_paged import (
+    BLOCK_SIZE,
+    CHUNKS_PER_LANE,
+    INDEX_HEAD_DIM,
+    K_STEPS,
+    KEYS_PER_NTILE,
+    MMA_M,
+    NTILES_IN_FLIGHT,
+    NTILES_PER_UNIT,
+    THREADS,
+    TOP_K_KERNEL_MAX,
+    _ceil_div,
+    _check_i32_1d,
+    _kbar_rows_view,
+    blocks_per_cta,
+    keys_per_warp,
+    query_row_map,
+    validate_params,
+)
+
+__all__ = [
+    "QsaScorePagedRecipe",
+    "dsl_decline_reason",
+    "compile_qsa_score_paged",
+    "run_qsa_score_paged",
+]
+
+_FAKE_STREAM = None
+# Imported normally (not through the template loader), so the module names its own source identity: ``template_key`` joins
+# it with a compile site's key to name the persistent object (``compiled_cache``); the cache's environment manifest covers
+# every other ``.py`` the kernel is traced from.
+FROST_SOURCE_DIGEST = hashlib.sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
+_CHUNK_BYTES = 16  # one 16-byte granule of a row: 8 bf16 = 4 words = one cp.async / ld.global.v4 / ld.shared.v4
+_WORDS_PER_CHUNK = 4
+_ROW_BYTES = INDEX_HEAD_DIM * 2  # 256 B per compressed row
+_SLOT_BYTES = KEYS_PER_NTILE * _ROW_BYTES  # one n-tile of 8 rows in the ring: 2 KiB
+_SLOT_ELEMS = _SLOT_BYTES // 4
+_A_TILE_BYTES = MMA_M * _ROW_BYTES  # one m-tile of the padded query tile: 16 rows x 256 B
+_A_TILE_ELEMS = _A_TILE_BYTES // 4
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- the kernel
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _page_word(tb_row: cutlass.Int64, k: cutlass.Int32, n_blocks_max: cutlass.Int32, rows_per_page: cutlass.Constexpr[int]) -> cutlass.Int32:
+    """The table word of compressed row ``k`` (a row past the capacity indexes a real word: ``n_blocks_max - 1``)."""
+    kc = k if k < n_blocks_max else n_blocks_max - cutlass.Int32(1)
+    pg = kc >> cutlass.Int32(rows_per_page.bit_length() - 1)
+    return ld_global(tb_row + pg.to(cutlass.Int64) * cutlass.Int64(4), cutlass.Int32)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _mul_wide_s32(a: cutlass.Int32, b: cutlass.Int32) -> cutlass.Int64:
+    """``mul.wide.s32``: one IMAD.WIDE for a 32 x 32 -> 64-bit product (a page index x a page stride in bytes)."""
+    return inline_ptx("mul.wide.s32 $0, $1, $2;", write_only_types=[cutlass.Int64], read_only_args=[a, b])
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _copy_ntile(
+    dst_lane: cutlass.Int64,
+    src_lane_off: cutlass.Int32,
+    kb_base: cutlass.Int64,
+    kb_page_bytes: cutlass.Int32,
+    word: cutlass.Int32,
+    num_pages: cutlass.Int32,
+    k_tile0: cutlass.Int32,
+    policy: cutlass.Int64,
+    rows_per_page: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+):
+    """The n-tile's 8 compressed rows into one ring slot, PAGE PART by page part (``min(R, 8)`` rows of one page): per part ONE
+    shuffle (the part's table word from the lane that read it -- a constant source lane), one validity check, one ``mul.wide``
+    page address; then ``rows / 2`` ``cp.async.cg`` of 16 B per lane at immediate offsets -- instruction ``e`` copies rows ``2 e``
+    (lanes 0-15) and ``2 e + 1`` (lanes 16-31), each row's two 128-B halves by eight consecutive lanes (whole lines per request).
+    A part on a ``-1`` / out-of-range page is ZERO-FILLED (``src-size 0``: nothing of the cache is read; the address is page 0, a
+    real row, either way).  A row at or past the visible count or the capacity reads a real row (its table word was clamped to
+    the capacity) and is never stored: its products stay in its own accumulator column."""
+    rows_pp = min(rows_per_page, KEYS_PER_NTILE)
+    zero_i = cutlass.Int32(0)
+    for part in cutlass.range_constexpr(KEYS_PER_NTILE // rows_pp):
+        w = cute.arch.shuffle_sync(word, 4 * part * rows_pp)  # the word of the part's first row sits in lanes 4 r .. 4 r + 3
+        ok = (w >= zero_i) & (w < num_pages)
+        page_c = w if ok else zero_i
+        size = cutlass.Int32(_CHUNK_BYTES) if ok else zero_i
+        row_off = ((k_tile0 + cutlass.Int32(part * rows_pp)) & cutlass.Int32(rows_per_page - 1)) * cutlass.Int32(
+            _ROW_BYTES
+        )  # the part's first row inside its page
+        src = kb_base + _mul_wide_s32(page_c, kb_page_bytes) + (row_off + src_lane_off).to(cutlass.Int64)
+        dst = dst_lane + cutlass.Int64(part * rows_pp * _ROW_BYTES)
+        for e in cutlass.range_constexpr(rows_pp // 2):
+            # every cp.async gets its OWN address registers (an opaque offset, never base + immediate): four back-to-back LDGSTS on one
+            # base register serialised on the register scoreboard under HBM latency (2x at B 32 x 128K, measured 2026-10-21)
+            off_e = opaque_i32(cutlass.Int32(e * 2 * _ROW_BYTES)).to(cutlass.Int64)
+            inline_ptx(
+                "cp.async.cg.shared.global.L2::cache_hint [$0], [$1], 16, $2, $3;", write_only_types=[], read_only_args=[dst + off_e, src + off_e, size, policy]
+            )
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _read_key_frags(sK, slot_elems: cutlass.Int32, g: cutlass.Int32, qd: cutlass.Int32):
+    """Lane ``(g, q)``'s B fragments of the n-tile in the ring slot: row ``g``'s granules ``q + 4 j`` (one ``ld.shared.v4`` each,
+    at the swizzled granule ``c ^ (4 x (g & 1))``) -- the 16 words the 8 k-steps consume."""
+    swz = (g & cutlass.Int32(1)) * cutlass.Int32(4)
+    row = slot_elems + g * cutlass.Int32(_ROW_BYTES // 4)
+    out = []
+    for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(CHUNKS_PER_LANE):
+        c_swz = (qd + cutlass.Int32(4 * j)) ^ swz
+        v = sK.load(row + c_swz * cutlass.Int32(_WORDS_PER_CHUNK), vector_size=4, alignment=16).to_elements()
+        for x in cutlass.range_constexpr(_WORDS_PER_CHUNK):
+            out.append(v[x])
+    return out[0], out[1], out[2], out[3], out[4], out[5], out[6], out[7], out[8], out[9], out[10], out[11], out[12], out[13], out[14], out[15]
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _copy_query_tile(
+    sA_tile: cutlass.Int64,
+    q_base: cutlass.Int64,
+    q_s0: cutlass.Int64,
+    q_s1: cutlass.Int64,
+    t0: cutlass.Int32,
+    tidx: cutlass.Int32,
+    t: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    s_q: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    h_i: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+):
+    """m-tile ``t`` of the padded (s, h) query tile into the CTA's SMEM staging: 16 rows x 256 B by the 128 threads in two
+    ``cp.async.cg`` instructions (thread ``tidx`` copies granule ``tidx % 16`` of rows ``tidx / 16`` and ``8 + tidx / 16``: sixteen
+    consecutive lanes per row, whole lines); a padding row (``h >= H_i`` inside the power of two, ``s >= S_q``) is ZERO-FILLED
+    (``src-size 0``; its address is a real row).  The destination granule is ``c ^ (4 x (row & 1))``, the fragment reads' swizzle."""
+    rm = query_row_map(s_q, h_i)
+    zero_i = cutlass.Int32(0)
+    s_q_i = cutlass.Int32(s_q)
+    h_i_i = cutlass.Int32(h_i)
+    c = tidx & cutlass.Int32(15)
+    g = tidx >> cutlass.Int32(4)  # the row within the half: 0..7
+    for half in cutlass.range_constexpr(2):
+        if cutlass.const_expr(rm.tile_rows == 1):
+            s_row = cutlass.Int32(t * rm.queries_per_tile + 8 * half) + g
+            h_row = zero_i
+        else:
+            s_row = cutlass.Int32((t // rm.tiles_per_query) * rm.queries_per_tile) + (g >> cutlass.Int32(rm.stages))
+            h_row = cutlass.Int32(16 * (t % rm.tiles_per_query) + half) + (g & cutlass.Int32(rm.group - 1)) * cutlass.Int32(2)
+        valid = (s_row < s_q_i) & (h_row < h_i_i)
+        s_c = s_row if s_row < s_q_i else s_q_i - cutlass.Int32(1)
+        h_c = h_row if h_row < h_i_i else h_i_i - cutlass.Int32(1)
+        src = (
+            q_base + ((t0 + s_c).to(cutlass.Int64) * q_s0 + h_c.to(cutlass.Int64) * q_s1) * cutlass.Int64(2) + c.to(cutlass.Int64) * cutlass.Int64(_CHUNK_BYTES)
+        )
+        dst = sA_tile + (
+            cutlass.Int32(half * 8 * _ROW_BYTES)
+            + g * cutlass.Int32(_ROW_BYTES)
+            + (c ^ ((g & cutlass.Int32(1)) * cutlass.Int32(4))) * cutlass.Int32(_CHUNK_BYTES)
+        ).to(cutlass.Int64)
+        size = cutlass.Int32(_CHUNK_BYTES) if valid else zero_i
+        inline_ptx("cp.async.cg.shared.global [$0], [$1], 16, $2;", write_only_types=[], read_only_args=[dst, src, size])
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _read_query_frags(sA, tile_elems: cutlass.Int32, g: cutlass.Int32, qd: cutlass.Int32, half: cutlass.Constexpr[int]):
+    """Lane ``(g, q)``'s A fragments of one half (rows ``g`` / ``g + 8``) of an m-tile: granules ``q + 4 j`` of the row (one
+    ``ld.shared.v4`` each at the swizzled granule ``c ^ (4 x (row & 1))``) -- the 16 words the 8 k-steps consume."""
+    row = cutlass.Int32(half * 8) + g
+    swz = (row & cutlass.Int32(1)) * cutlass.Int32(4)
+    base = tile_elems + row * cutlass.Int32(_ROW_BYTES // 4)
+    out = []
+    for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(CHUNKS_PER_LANE):
+        c_swz = (qd + cutlass.Int32(4 * j)) ^ swz
+        v = sA.load(base + c_swz * cutlass.Int32(_WORDS_PER_CHUNK), vector_size=4, alignment=16).to_elements()
+        for x in cutlass.range_constexpr(_WORDS_PER_CHUNK):
+            out.append(v[x])
+    return out[0], out[1], out[2], out[3], out[4], out[5], out[6], out[7], out[8], out[9], out[10], out[11], out[12], out[13], out[14], out[15]
+
+
+@cute.kernel
+def frost_qsa_score_paged(
+    mQ: cute.Tensor,  # [T, H_i, D] bf16; token / head strides symbolic (Int64), D contiguous
+    mKbar: cute.Tensor,  # [num_pages, R, D] bf16; page / row strides symbolic (Int64), D contiguous
+    mTable: cute.Tensor,  # [B, max_pages] int32; row stride symbolic (Int64), unit column stride
+    mKvLens: cute.Tensor,  # [B] int32, contiguous
+    mLogits: cute.Tensor,  # [T, n_blocks_max] fp32; row stride symbolic (Int64), unit column stride
+    mCounts: cute.Tensor,  # [T] int32, contiguous
+    mBlockLens: Optional[cute.Tensor],  # [T] int32, contiguous, or None (folded out)
+    top_k: cutlass.Int32,
+    scale: cutlass.Float32,
+    h_i: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    s_q: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    rows_per_page: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    units_per_warp: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    ring_depth: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    use_pdl: cutlass.Constexpr[bool],
+) -> None:
+    """One CTA = chunk ``blockIdx.x`` of ``blocks_per_cta`` compressed rows of sequence ``blockIdx.y``, four independent warps of
+    ``keys_per_warp`` rows each (module docstring)."""
+    if cutlass.const_expr(use_pdl):
+        wait_on_dependent_grids()
+    rm = query_row_map(s_q, h_i)  # the (s, h) -> MMA-row map (host facts, compile-time)
+    n_tiles = NTILES_PER_UNIT * units_per_warp  # n-tiles of 8 keys per warp
+    depth = ring_depth  # n-tiles of keys in flight (cp.async groups) ahead of the MMAs
+    ring_slots = min(
+        ring_depth + 1, n_tiles
+    )  # + the slot being read (the one warp sync per n-tile orders the WAR on the slot reused next); no spare when no mainloop copy exists
+    # the two SMEM buffers (declared ahead of every branch): each warp's ring of ring_slots n-tiles of 8 compressed rows, and the
+    # CTA's padded (s, h) query tile (16 rows x 256 B per m-tile), both written by cp.async and read as fragments
+    sK = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int32, THREADS // 32 * ring_slots * _SLOT_ELEMS, alignment=128, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem)
+    sA = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int32, rm.m_tiles * _A_TILE_ELEMS, alignment=128, space=cutlass.AddressSpace.smem)
+    n_groups = rm.m_tiles // rm.tiles_per_query  # query groups per lane at P' >= 2 (one head-sum each)
+    has_lens = cutlass.const_expr(mBlockLens is not None)
+    pair_rows = cutlass.const_expr(rm.tile_rows > 1)  # the lane's two rows are two heads of ONE query (else two queries)
+    tidx = cutlass.Int32(cute.arch.thread_idx()[0])
+    lane = tidx & cutlass.Int32(31)
+    warp = tidx >> cutlass.Int32(5)
+    g = lane >> cutlass.Int32(2)  # the MMA group id: the A / C rows g and g + 8, the B key n = g
+    qd = lane & cutlass.Int32(3)  # the thread in the quad: chunks q + 4 j, the C keys 2q and 2q + 1
+    bidx, bidy, _ = cute.arch.block_idx()
+    chunk_id = cutlass.Int32(bidx)
+    b = cutlass.Int32(bidy)
+    n_blocks_max = cutlass.Int32(mLogits.shape[1])
+    num_pages = cutlass.Int32(mKbar.shape[0])
+    four = cutlass.Int64(4)  # int32 / fp32 bytes
+    b64 = b.to(cutlass.Int64)
+    zero_i = cutlass.Int32(0)
+    s_q_i = cutlass.Int32(s_q)
+    h_i_i = cutlass.Int32(h_i)

@@ -0,0 +1,430 @@
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""``qsa_select_paged`` -- block selection for a DECODE step over the PAGED compressed-key cache: the DSL-free host entry of the
+paged decode scorer (``kernels/qsa_score_paged.py``) and the host-side facts of that kernel.
+
+A decode step of a block-sparse (``QsaSpec``) layer scores each of its ``S_q`` query rows per sequence against the compressed
+keys of the complete 4-token blocks the row can see, and the top-k of those scores is the row's block list.  The serving
+stacks keep the compressed keys PAGED on the main block table (one compressed row per 4 tokens, ``page_size / 4`` rows per
+page); the scorer kernel reads them there and the deterministic radix top-k follows -- two launches, no torch prologue::
+
+    pos_t   = kv_lens[b] - S_q + s                       (row s of sequence b; t = b * S_q + s)
+    n_vis_t = clamp(floor((pos_t + 1) / 4), 0, n_blocks_max)
+    logits[t, j] = scale * sum_h relu(qi[t, h] . kbar[b, j])        for j < n_vis_t, kbar[b, j] = cache[table[b, j // R], j % R]
+    counts[t]     = n_vis_t                                          (R = page_size / 4 compressed rows per page)
+    block_lens[t] = min(top_k, n_vis_t)
+    block_ids[t]  = the top_k of logits[t, :counts[t]], ASCENDING, -1 past block_lens[t]
+
+**Placement (Rule 7).**  This module imports no CuTe DSL -- torch, the stream helpers and the version gates only -- so the
+documented import path resolves on every installed DSL, the public 4.6.2 wheel (the floor vLLM and SGLang pin) included.
+:func:`qsa_select_decode_paged` checks every operand's FORM first, then gates the DSL floor, the ``sm_107a`` target on cc 10.7
+and the radix top-k's cc 9.0 -- each a typed ``NotImplementedError`` naming the version or the device -- and only THEN imports
+the kernel module (whose import executes the DSL, like its neighbours) inside the function body.  The kernel's host-side
+facts a declaration may need before any kernel is reached -- the MMA row map of the query rows, the compile-key validator, the
+knob defaults, the byte model -- live here for the same reason, and the kernel module imports them from here (never the other way
+round at module scope).  The kernel's SMEM table, barrier table, PDL sites and degenerate-input matrix are in the kernel
+module's docstring; :func:`qsa_select_decode_paged` documents the selection's contract.
+
+**Streams (Rule 5).**  The call resolves ONE torch stream from ``stream`` first (:func:`cudnn._torch_stream.launch_stream`: a
+``torch.cuda.Stream``, a raw handle or a ``cuda.CUstream``; ``None`` = torch's current stream on the operands' device) and
+runs every torch operation inside its context -- the scorer's output allocations, the scorer launch, the top-k wrapper's own
+output and scratch allocations and its launch -- handing both kernels that stream's raw handle.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import NamedTuple, Optional
+
+import torch
+
+from cudnn._torch_stream import launch_stream, stream_context
+from cudnn.api_base import TupleDict
+from cudnn.frost.buffers import cutedsl_arch_requirement_error, cutedsl_requirement_error
+
+__all__ = [
+    "qsa_select_decode_paged",
+    "INDEX_HEAD_DIM",
+    "BLOCK_SIZE",
+    "QSA_TOP_K",
+    "TOP_K_KERNEL_MAX",
+    "MAX_QUERY_ROWS",

+class _Case:
+    """One decode step over a paged cache: ``batch`` sequences, ``s_q`` rows each, a shuffled page table into a pool with spare
+    pages, and the fp64 reference through the SAME table (independent of the kernel's addressing)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, batch, s_q, n_blocks_max, page_size, kv_lens, *, seed, h=H, extra_pages=5):
+        self.batch, self.s_q, self.n_blocks_max, self.page_size, self.h = batch, s_q, n_blocks_max, page_size, h
+        self.rpp = page_size // BS
+        self.max_pages = -(-n_blocks_max // self.rpp)
+        g = torch.Generator(device=_DEV).manual_seed(seed)
+        self.qi = torch.randn(batch * s_q, h, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=_DEV, generator=g)
+        self.num_pages = batch * self.max_pages + extra_pages
+        self.pool = torch.randn(self.num_pages, self.rpp, 1, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=_DEV, generator=g)
+        self.table = torch.randperm(self.num_pages, device=_DEV, generator=g)[: batch * self.max_pages].view(batch, self.max_pages).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
+        self.kv_lens = torch.tensor(list(kv_lens), dtype=torch.int32, device=_DEV)
+        assert self.kv_lens.numel() == batch
+
+    def dense(self, table=None):
+        """``[B, n_blocks_max, D]`` bf16: the compressed keys gathered through the table (a ``-1`` / out-of-range page -> zeros)."""
+        table = self.table if table is None else table
+        idx = table.long()
+        ok = (idx >= 0) & (idx < self.num_pages)
+        rows = self.pool.select(2, 0)[idx.clamp(0, self.num_pages - 1).view(-1)].view(self.batch, self.max_pages, self.rpp, D)
+        rows = torch.where(ok.view(self.batch, self.max_pages, 1, 1), rows, torch.zeros_like(rows))
+        return rows.reshape(self.batch, self.max_pages * self.rpp, D)[:, : self.n_blocks_max]
+
+    def positions(self):
+        return (self.kv_lens.long() - self.s_q)[:, None] + torch.arange(self.s_q, device=_DEV)[None, :]
+
+    def n_vis(self):
+        return torch.div(self.positions() + 1, BS, rounding_mode="floor").clamp(0, self.n_blocks_max)
+
+    def reference(self, scale, table=None):
+        """fp64 ``[B, s_q, n_blocks_max]``, ``-inf`` at or past the row's visible count."""
+        q = self.qi.view(self.batch, self.s_q, self.h, D).double()
+        scores = torch.relu(torch.einsum("brhd,bnd->brhn", q, self.dense(table).double())).sum(dim=2) * scale
+        visible = torch.arange(self.n_blocks_max, device=_DEV).view(1, 1, -1) < self.n_vis().view(self.batch, self.s_q, 1)
+        return scores.masked_fill(~visible, float("-inf"))
+
+    def outputs(self, with_lens=True):
+        t, dev = self.batch * self.s_q, self.qi.device  # the operands' device, whichever device is current at the call
+        logits = torch.full((t, self.n_blocks_max), SENTINEL, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
+        counts = torch.full((t,), -7, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+        lens = torch.full((t,), -7, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev) if with_lens else None
+        return logits, counts, lens
+
+    def run(self, recipe, *, table=None, top_k=TOP_K, scale=None, with_lens=True):
+        logits, counts, lens = self.outputs(with_lens)
+        sp.run_qsa_score_paged(
+            recipe,
+            self.qi,
+            self.pool,
+            self.table if table is None else table,
+            self.kv_lens,
+            logits,
+            counts,
+            lens,
+            top_k=top_k,
+            scale=D**-0.5 if scale is None else scale,
+            stream=_stream(),
+        )
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        return logits, counts, lens
+

+def _bits(x):
+    return x.view(torch.int32)

+def _assert_scorer(case, logits, counts, lens, *, top_k=TOP_K, scale=None, table=None):
+    """The scorer's contract on one case: counts = the oracle's visible count per row, block_lens = min(top_k, counts), every visible
+    column within the fp32 budget of the fp64 reference, every other column still the sentinel."""
+    scale = D**-0.5 if scale is None else scale
+    n_vis = case.n_vis()
+    _, want_counts = full_block_ids(case.positions(), case.n_blocks_max, BS)  # the oracle's count rule at the capacity: min(capacity, floor((p + 1) / 4))
+    assert torch.equal(counts, want_counts.view(-1).to(torch.int32)), "counts differ from the oracle's count rule"
+    assert torch.equal(counts, n_vis.view(-1).to(torch.int32))
+    if lens is not None:
+        assert torch.equal(lens, torch.minimum(counts, torch.full_like(counts, top_k))), "block_lens differs from min(top_k, counts)"
+    ref = case.reference(scale, table)
+    for b in range(case.batch):
+        for s in range(case.s_q):
+            n = int(n_vis[b, s])
+            row = logits[b * case.s_q + s]
+            if n:
+                torch.testing.assert_close(
+                    row[:n].double(), ref[b, s, :n], atol=LOGIT_ATOL, rtol=LOGIT_RTOL, msg=f"sequence {b} row {s}: logits off the fp64 reference"
+                )
+            assert bool((row[n:] == SENTINEL).all()), f"sequence {b} row {s}: a column at or past the visible count {n} was written"
+
+
+def _assert_rows(block_ids, scores, block_lens, ref, top_k, tie_tol=TIE_TOL):
+    """Per row of ``ref [rows, n_blocks_max]`` (the dense decode selector's oracle): the valid count equals ``block_lens`` =
+    ``min(top_k, visible)``, ids are unique local ids below the visible count, the scores are the reference scores of the selected
+    ids (fp32 of an fp64 value), and the SET equals torch.topk's up to flips within ``tie_tol`` of the k-th reference score."""
+    rows, n_blocks_max = ref.shape
+    assert block_ids.shape == scores.shape == (rows, top_k)
+    assert block_ids.dtype == torch.int32 and scores.dtype == torch.float32 and block_lens.dtype == torch.int32
+    valid = block_ids >= 0
+    visible = torch.isfinite(ref).sum(dim=-1)
+    assert torch.equal(valid.sum(dim=-1).to(torch.int32), block_lens), "the valid prefix differs from block_lens"
+    assert torch.equal(block_lens.long(), visible.clamp(max=top_k)), "block_lens differs from min(top_k, visible)"
+    prefix = torch.arange(top_k, device=ref.device)[None, :] < block_lens[:, None].long()
+    assert torch.equal(valid, prefix), "the valid ids are not a prefix followed by -1"
+    assert bool(((block_ids < visible[:, None]) | ~valid).all()), "an id at or past the row's visible count"
+    assert bool(torch.isneginf(scores[~valid]).all())
+    row_idx = torch.arange(rows, device=ref.device).unsqueeze(1).expand_as(block_ids)
+    gathered = ref[row_idx[valid], block_ids[valid].long()]
+    torch.testing.assert_close(scores[valid].double(), gathered, atol=tie_tol, rtol=tie_tol)
+    in_actual = torch.zeros_like(ref, dtype=torch.bool)
+    in_actual[row_idx[valid], block_ids[valid].long()] = True
+    assert torch.equal(in_actual.sum(dim=-1), valid.sum(dim=-1)), "a row lists a block twice"
+    k_eff = min(top_k, n_blocks_max)
+    ref_topk = torch.topk(ref, k_eff, dim=-1)
+    exp_valid = torch.isfinite(ref_topk.values)
+    in_expected = torch.zeros_like(in_actual)
+    rows_k = torch.arange(rows, device=ref.device).unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, k_eff)
+    in_expected[rows_k[exp_valid], ref_topk.indices[exp_valid]] = True
+    kth = torch.where(exp_valid, ref_topk.values, torch.full_like(ref_topk.values, float("inf"))).min(dim=-1).values
+    differs = in_actual ^ in_expected
+    if bool(differs.any()):
+        gap = (ref - kth.unsqueeze(1)).abs()[differs]
+        assert bool((gap <= tie_tol).all()), f"{int(differs.sum())} ids differ from torch.topk beyond a tie (max gap {float(gap.max()):.3e})"
+
+
+def _assert_canonical(block_ids, block_lens):
+    """The selected ids come back in ASCENDING order (the deterministic radix kernel's canonical order), the padding last."""
+    for r in range(block_ids.shape[0]):
+        n = int(block_lens[r])
+        ids = block_ids[r, :n]
+        assert bool((ids[1:] > ids[:-1]).all()), f"row {r}: the selected ids are not strictly ascending"
+        assert bool((block_ids[r, n:] == -1).all()), f"row {r}: a non -1 entry past block_lens"
+
+
+def _step_kv_lens(n_blocks_max, rows, batch=4):
+    """Step-0 positions covering every residue modulo the block size, the last sequence seeing every block of the cache."""
+    base = BS * n_blocks_max - rows - 3
+    return [max(0, base + r) + rows for r in range(batch)]

+    down the ``bypassed`` branch (a plain trace per process, no persistent object, no in-process memo).  The site passes that key and
+    its symbol and leaves no bare ``cute.compile(``."""

+    assert cc.template_key(vars(sp), {"key": key}, "compile_qsa_score_paged") == f"{sp.FROST_SOURCE_DIGEST}|compile_qsa_score_paged|[('key', {key!r})]"
+    src = Path(sp.__file__).read_text()
+    assert "cute.compile(" not in src and 'symbol="cudnn_block_qsa_score_paged"' in src and '"compile_qsa_score_paged")' in src
+
+
+@needs_cuda
+def test_front_door_declines_by_version_in_a_fresh_process_without_importing_the_kernel_module():
+    """Rule 7 at the DOCUMENTED import path, in a fresh interpreter (in this process the kernel module is already imported, so an in-process
+    check would pass for the wrong reason).  The installed DSL is modeled as the public 4.6.2 wheel two ways at once -- the version
+    discovery answers 4.6.2 AND ``cutlass.experimental`` (the 4.7.0-only API every tile_dsl helper imports at module scope) is made
+    unimportable -- then the front door is imported and the selector called on real CUDA operands: the import touched neither the kernel
+    module nor ``cudnn.frost.tile_dsl``, the call raises the typed ``NotImplementedError`` naming the floor and the found version, and
+    afterwards the kernel module, ``cudnn.frost.tile_dsl`` and the radix top-k's package are still not imported."""
+    probe = r"""
+import importlib.abc
+import sys
+
+
+class _NoExperimental(importlib.abc.MetaPathFinder):
+    # the public 4.6.2 wheel has no cutlass.experimental: an import of it from inside the DSL is the untyped failure Rule 7 forbids
+    def find_spec(self, fullname, path=None, target=None):
+        if fullname == "cutlass.experimental" or fullname.startswith("cutlass.experimental."):
+            raise ModuleNotFoundError("No module named 'cutlass.experimental' (modeled: the public 4.6.2 wheel)")
+        return None
+
+
+sys.meta_path.insert(0, _NoExperimental())
+import torch
+import cudnn.frost.buffers as buffers
+
+buffers._DSL_STATE = (True, ("nvidia-cutlass-dsl", "4.6.2"))
+from cudnn.gated_attention_block import qsa_select_paged as fd
+
+KERNEL = "cudnn.gated_attention_block.kernels.qsa_score_paged"
+assert KERNEL not in sys.modules, "importing the front door imported the kernel module"
+assert "cudnn.frost.tile_dsl" not in sys.modules, "importing the front door imported tile_dsl"
+qi = torch.zeros(1, 4, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+pool = torch.zeros(3, 4, 1, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+table = torch.tensor([[0, 1]], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+kv_lens = torch.tensor([9], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+try:
+    fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(qi, pool, table, kv_lens, seq_q=1)
+except NotImplementedError as error:
+    assert "qsa_select_decode_paged requires nvidia-cutlass-dsl >= 4.7.0; found 4.6.2" in str(error), str(error)
+else:
+    raise AssertionError("the selector ran on a sub-floor DSL")
+assert KERNEL not in sys.modules, "the decline imported the kernel module"
+assert "cudnn.frost.tile_dsl" not in sys.modules, "the decline imported tile_dsl"
+assert not any(m.startswith("cudnn.deepseek_sparse_attention") for m in sys.modules), "the decline imported the radix top-k's package"
+print("@@FRONT_DOOR_OK")
+"""
+    run = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", probe], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900)
+    assert run.returncode == 0, f"rc {run.returncode}\n{run.stderr[-3000:]}"
+    assert "@@FRONT_DOOR_OK" in run.stdout, run.stdout[-2000:]
+
+
+@needs_cuda
+def test_rule7_gates_run_before_any_compile(monkeypatch):
+    """The DSL floor, then the sm_107a target, then the radix top-k's and PDL's cc 9.0: each a NotImplementedError that names the
+    version or the device, raised by the compile entry (the kernel module's own gate) and by the selector (the front door's gate)
+    BEFORE any kernel is compiled or imported -- each module's binding patched, since each gates for itself."""
+    case = _Case(1, 1, 8, 16, [9], seed=1)
+    kw = dict(seq_q=1)
+    for mod in (sp, fd):
+        monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "cutedsl_requirement_error", lambda what: f"{what} requires nvidia-cutlass-dsl >= 4.7.0; found 4.6.2")
+    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match="qsa_score_paged requires nvidia-cutlass-dsl >= 4.7.0; found 4.6.2"):
+        sp.compile_qsa_score_paged(h_i=H, s_q=1, page_size=16)
+    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match="qsa_select_decode_paged requires nvidia-cutlass-dsl >= 4.7.0; found 4.6.2"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, **kw)
+    for mod in (sp, fd):
+        monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "cutedsl_requirement_error", lambda what: None)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(
+            mod, "cutedsl_arch_requirement_error", lambda cc: "SM107 requires a CuTe DSL build supporting sm_107a; found 4.7.0 without that target"
+        )
+    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match="sm_107a"):
+        sp.compile_qsa_score_paged(h_i=H, s_q=1, page_size=16)
+    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match="sm_107a"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, **kw)
+    for mod in (sp, fd):
+        monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "cutedsl_arch_requirement_error", lambda cc: None)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(sp, "compute_capability", lambda dev: (8, 0))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "get_device_capability", lambda device=None: (8, 0))
+    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match=r"cc 9\.0 or later; found cc 8\.0"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, **kw)
+    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match=r"griddepcontrol.*cc 8\.0"):
+        sp.compile_qsa_score_paged(h_i=H, s_q=1, page_size=16, use_pdl=True)
+
+
+@needs_cuda
+def test_e4m3_pair_is_refused_by_name_and_a_mixed_pair_is_a_form_error():
+    case = _Case(1, 1, 8, 16, [9], seed=2)
+    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match="e4m3"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi.to(_E4M3), case.pool.to(_E4M3), case.table, case.kv_lens, seq_q=1)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="both be bfloat16"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi.to(_E4M3), case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, seq_q=1)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="both be bfloat16"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool.to(_E4M3), case.table, case.kv_lens, seq_q=1)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="both be bfloat16"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi.half(), case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, seq_q=1)
+
+
+@needs_cuda
+def test_selector_form_checks_name_the_fault():
+    """Every form check fires ahead of the gates and the compile (no kernel runs for a malformed call)."""
+    case = _Case(2, 2, 16, 16, [9, 40], seed=3)
+    kw = dict(seq_q=2)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=r"head_dim 128"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi[..., :64], case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, **kw)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="T must be B x seq_q"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, seq_q=3)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="seq_q must be >= 1"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, seq_q=0)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="multiple of 8"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, n_blocks_max=12, **kw)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="top_k must be in"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, top_k=0, **kw)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="top_k must be in"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, top_k=fd.TOP_K_KERNEL_MAX + 1, **kw)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="scale must be positive"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens, scale=0.0, **kw)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="block_table must be an int32"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table.to(torch.int64), case.kv_lens, **kw)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="block_table needs a unit column stride"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table.t().contiguous().t(), case.kv_lens, **kw)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=r"kv_lens must be an int32 \[2\]"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens.to(torch.int64), **kw)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=r"kv_lens must be an int32 \[2\]"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, case.kv_lens[:1], **kw)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="kv_lens must be contiguous"):
+        fd.qsa_select_decode_paged(case.qi, case.pool, case.table, torch.stack([case.kv_lens, case.kv_lens], 1)[:, 0], **kw)
+    if torch.cuda.device_count() > 1:
+        other_dev = torch.device("cuda", 1 if torch.device(_DEV).index in (None, 0) else 0)
